# MyChrome

> MyChrome is a local MCP server and native macOS app that lets an AI assistant help in the user's existing Google Chrome. It preserves the working page and login context, reads through Chrome Apple Events, and uses real mouse and keyboard input. No extension or debugging port is required.

## Product and setup

- [Product website](https://shuaige121.github.io/mychrome-mcp/): purpose, controls, requirements and compatibility.
- [Getting started](https://shuaige121.github.io/mychrome-mcp/getting-started.html): source installation, permissions, client connection and a local practice task.
- [FAQ](https://shuaige121.github.io/mychrome-mcp/faq.html): data handling, clients, controls and website limits.
- [中文网站](https://shuaige121.github.io/mychrome-mcp/zh/): 中文介绍与安装入口。
- [Source](https://github.com/shuaige121/mychrome-mcp): MIT-licensed source and release notes.

## Capability boundaries

- Apple Silicon, macOS 13+, Google Chrome in /Applications, supported Node.js and Xcode Command Line Tools. Node 24+ is recommended; 20.19+ and 22.13+ are also supported.
- Install with `bash scripts/setup.sh` from a source checkout. This release is not published to npm.
- Codex and Claude Code support browser tools. Live assistant text and replies in the native app need a supported Codex integration and associated thread. Claude has no live text/direct reply adapter there.
- Use the explicit existing tab when requested; confirm the website account before changes. Public pages may be better handled through an API or web fetch.
- Physical input is serialized. During takeover, ordinary user input is intercepted; double Esc cancels the active agent. Global pause prevents subsequent input. Stop does not undo actions already sent.
- Website routine recording is on by default. Local metadata may reveal usage context; typed and selected values are not saved as replay defaults. Runs need fresh parameters and an explicit tab, stop on mismatches, and do not prove the broader task succeeded.
- Page content returned through MCP goes to the AI client and is handled under its settings. Local operation is not a promise that all task data remains on-device.
- Login, CAPTCHA and access challenges belong to the user. No universal website compatibility or bypass guarantee.
- Verify the visible result after a change; do not infer success from a tool finishing.

This file is a concise reading guide. It does not claim search ranking or inclusion in AI answers.
